builder_plan.scenario: Your coding assistant makes changes that still need substantial repair before merging.
builder_plan.change: Try the technique on held-out issues from a repository with reliable tests.
builder_plan.baseline: The same coding agent, repository snapshot, tools, and token budget.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Correct patches, regression failures, human repair time, and total cost per accepted change.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Reva: Real-Time Vulnerability Detection through Contextual Probing of Large Language Models
summary: REVA replaces multi-call agentic vulnerability-detection loops (tool runs, hypothesis testing, iterative reasoning) with a single forward pass whose prompt includes a pre-computed module threat model, static-analysis findings, and call-graph data, read by a trained linear probe on the LLM's internal representations. The cost is offline infrastructure to build per-module threat models and call graphs, a trained probe per backbone model, and access to hidden states, which excludes most closed third-party APIs and ties the probe to a specific open model that fits on one 24 GB GPU. It can fail on code whose risk depends on cross-module context the pre-computed summary omits, the probe may not transfer across model versions or languages, and 60% accuracy on PrimeVul implies substantial false-positive and false-negative rates unsuitable as a sole gate.
rationale: The approach is reproducible with a single-GPU open model and a small trained probe, but it requires building static-analysis and probing infrastructure and validating accuracy on the reader's own codebase before production use.
technique: Contextual probing of LLM hidden states for vulnerability detection

claims.statement: REVA replaces multi-call agentic vulnerability-detection loops (tool runs, hypothesis testing, iterative reasoning) with a single forward pass whose prompt includes a pre-computed module threat model, static-analysis findings, and call-graph data, read by a trained linear probe on the LLM's internal representations. The cost is offline infrastructure to build per-module threat models and call graphs, a trained probe per backbone model, and access to hidden states, which excludes most closed third-party APIs and ties the probe to a specific open model that fits on one 24 GB GPU. It can fail on code whose risk depends on cross-module context the pre-computed summary omits, the probe may not transfer across model versions or languages, and 60% accuracy on PrimeVul implies substantial false-positive and false-negative rates unsuitable as a sole gate.

On PrimeVul, REVA on GLM-5.3-Flash reaches 60.0% accuracy in about one second per function, matching the agentic detector VulTriage (59.2%) while being over 250 times faster and less than a tenth as costly; the probe is 14-17% more accurate than the LLM's direct verdict on the same prompt.
